---
title: "ML in Life Sciences"
---
Machine learning in biology is a set of choices: what kind of task you have,
what model you use, and how you train and evaluate it. This site maps them out,
then walks through each one on real biological data.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  ML["What does your training data look like?"]
  ML --> S["<b>Supervised</b><br/>inputs + answers"]
  ML --> U["<b>Unsupervised</b><br/>inputs only"]
  ML --> SS["<b>Self-supervised</b><br/>model hides & predicts parts of input"]
  ML --> SEMI["<b>Semi-supervised</b><br/>few answers, many unlabeled"]
  ML --> RL["<b>Reinforcement</b><br/>actions + rewards"]
  S --> R["Regression<br/><i>disease progression</i>"]
  S --> C["Classification<br/><i>tumor malignancy</i>"]
  S --> SV["Time-to-event<br/><i>patient survival</i>"]
  S --> SL["Sequence labeling<br/><i>per-residue structure</i>"]
  U --> CL["Clustering<br/><i>cell types</i>"]
  U --> DR["Dimensionality reduction<br/><i>PCA on expression</i>"]
  U --> G["Generative / density<br/><i>denoising sequencing data</i>"]
  U --> AN["Anomaly detection<br/><i>contaminated samples</i>"]
  SS --> PLM["Pretraining<br/><i>protein language models</i>"]
  SEMI --> SP["<i>labeling slides</i>"]
  RL --> MD["<i>molecule design</i>"]
```
